preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)
Attacker must hold some Milesinu tokens to trigger fee collection

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setTaxFeePercent(), setDevFeePercent(), and setLiquidityFeePercent() with values exceeding 25% each (e.g., 30). Then perform a token transfer to trigger fee collection. The excessive fees will be collected in the contract and later distributed to the DevAddress (which you can control via setDevAddress()) and added to liquidity (benefiting the owner).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The Milesinu token contract allows the owner to set arbitrary fee percentages without any maximum limit. By setting all three fees (tax, liquidity, dev) to high values (e.g., 30% each), the owner can extract value from token transfers. When a transfer occurs, 90% of the amount goes to fees (30% each of three fees), which are then distributed: half of the swapped ETH goes to DevAddress (controlled by owner) and half is added to liquidity (benefiting owner through LP tokens).
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Set all fee percentages to 30% each. 3. Set DevAddress to attacker's address. 4. Enable swapAndLiquify. 5. Transfer tokens to trigger fee collection. 6. Profit from ETH sent to DevAddress.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner (need to find owner address first). 2. Call setTaxFeePercent(30), setLiquidityFeePercent(30), setDevFeePercent(30). 3. Call setDevAddress(payable(attacker)). 4. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(true). 5. Ensure attacker has some tokens (deal or transfer from owner). 6. Transfer tokens to another address to trigger fee collection. 7. Wait for fees to accumulate and be distributed. 8. Verify attacker's ETH balance increased.
